name: Algeria
fact: Spanning prehistoric rock art and dramatic sandstone forests, the vast plateau of Tassili n'Ajjer preserves thousands of ancient carvings that reveal the Sahara's lush green past.

name: Angola
fact: Angola gifted the world Kizomba music and dance, a soulful and captivating rhythm that has inspired dance communities across every continent.

name: Benin
fact: Built entirely upon wooden stilts over Lake Nokoué, the historic stilt village of Ganvié thrives as a vibrant community celebrating centuries of aquatic architectural ingenuity.

name: Botswana
fact: The inland oasis of the Okavango Delta sustains Africa's largest elephant population, flourishing through Botswana's pioneering model of low-impact, high-value wildlife ecotourism.

name: Burkina Faso
fact: Biennially hosting the celebrated FESPACO festival in Ouagadougou, the nation unites storytellers from across the globe as the proud capital of African cinema.

name: Burundi
fact: Burundi's iconic royal drummers perform mesmerizing polyrhythmic rituals recognized by UNESCO, weaving athletic choreography and thunderous beats into an internationally acclaimed art form.

name: Cabo Verde
fact: Cape Verde's soulful Morna musical tradition, championed globally by Cesária Évora, earned UNESCO recognition for its poignant poetry, acoustic harmonies, and profound emotional depth.

name: Cameroon
fact: Affectionately celebrated as 'Africa in miniature,' Cameroon encompasses every major climate and landscape of the continent, from lush equatorial rainforests to windswept volcanic peaks.

name: Central African Republic
fact: Dzanga-Sangha National Park features a legendary mineral clearing where hundreds of majestic forest elephants gather peacefully alongside western lowland gorillas amidst pristine tropical wilderness.

name: Chad
fact: Shimmering amidst the hyper-arid Sahara, the breathtaking Lakes of Ounianga form an extraordinary UNESCO-listed oasis fed continuously by ancient subterranean fossil water.

name: Comoros
fact: Known as the Perfume Isles, Comoros harvests fragrant ylang-ylang flowers that supply the global luxury fragrance industry with essential oils of unmatched purity.

name: Republic of the Congo
fact: Brazzaville earned recognition as the first African capital designated a UNESCO City of Music, celebrating a vibrant heritage of infectious Congolese rumba.

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
fact: Nestled within northeastern rainforests, the Okapi Wildlife Reserve protects the elusive striped forest giraffe and preserves vital tropical biodiversity found nowhere else on Earth.

name: Côte d'Ivoire
fact: As the world's leading producer of cocoa, Côte d'Ivoire supplies the essential foundation for premier artisan chocolatiers and confectioners around the globe.

name: Djibouti
fact: Coastal waters in the Gulf of Tadjoura provide a world-renowned haven where marine enthusiasts can swim alongside majestic whale sharks during their seasonal feeding migrations.

name: Egypt
fact: Harnessing abundant desert sunshine near Aswan, the colossal Benban Solar Park ranks among the world's largest photovoltaic installations, driving clean energy transition across North Africa.

name: Equatorial Guinea
fact: Monte Alén National Park preserves pristine tropical rainforests across rugged highlands, providing an essential ecological sanctuary for endangered western lowland gorillas and rare forest elephants.

name: Eritrea
fact: Asmara boasts a remarkably preserved modernist cityscape recognized by UNESCO, showcasing superb Art Deco cinemas, cafes, and futuristic architecture along palm-lined boulevards.

name: Eswatini
fact: Artisans at Ngwenya Glass craft internationally admired handmade sculptures and glassware entirely from recycled materials, supporting community conservation funds across the Kingdom.

name: Ethiopia
fact: Celebrated as the ancestral birthplace of Arabica coffee, Ethiopia shares an enduring gift with humanity through its elaborate and hospitality-centered traditional coffee ceremonies.

name: Gabon
fact: With over eighty percent of its territory blanketed in pristine rainforest, Gabon protects vast wilderness corridors that make it an essential global carbon sink.
